newsitem.title: GHANA: Plane heads for Freetown to evacuate Lebanese.
newsitem.headline: Plane heads for Freetown to evacuate Lebanese.

text.p: A Middle East Airlines Boeing 707 left Ghana for Sierra Leone on Wednesday to evacuate 150 Lebanese nationals after a weekend coup.
The airline's Ghana manager said the plane would also bring out the bodies of two Lebanese killed in the fighting.
"There are about 150 of my people waiting for us now at the (Freetown) airport. There are two bodies and one injured," said Issam Gharzeddine, the airline's manager in Ghana.
He said the plane would fly to Freetown's Lungi Airport, load the passengers and fly to Abidjan for refuelling before taking off for Beirut.
Many of the 2,000 Lebanese living in Sierra Leone, most of whom are businessmen, took shelter at the Lebanese embassy in Freetown.
About 400 foreign nationals crammed into hotels at Freetown's beachside Aberdeen district after soldiers who seized power on Sunday went on an orgy of looting.

Freetown's new strongman Major Johnny Paul Koromah and his ruling council on Wednesday met ambassadors and United Nations officials who are trying to organise an evacuation on a U.N.-chartered boat which arrived at the port on Tuesday.
U.N. officials said they planned to bring out non-essential staff, and would talk to Nigerian troops in Freetown about how to get them from the hotels to the port.
